title: Który przypadek?
note: CASE-SELECTION UNIT, the third of five (codex/WHICH-CASE-SPEC.md, JAMES-LOCKED 2026-08-07), sitting immediately before b1_case_gym [130]. TEACHES NOTHING NEW - teaches_structures [] and teaches_lemmas []; every form was checked against the position-aware pool for this node (make_pool.py --before b1_which_case, 2111 lemmas). INTRO TABLE IS DERIVED from data/case-map.json filtered to taught_by <= path 129 - eighteen rows, six cases. ONE CASE-MAP FIX IN THIS COMMIT, the same class as the two the A1 unit made: the Dative row read 'pomagam - dziekuje - daje' under taught_by b1_dative_sg [118], but that pack teaches only pomagac and dziekowac; dawac/oddawac land at b1_giving [120], whose own note records that b1_dative_sg explicitly deferred them. The row is now split - 'pomagam - dziekuje' at b1_dative_sg and 'daje - oddaje' at b1_giving, whose example is that pack's own verified sentence. Both are before this unit, so the derived table is unchanged; the fix is for the Przypadki panel, which would otherwise have shown daje to a learner two units before he meets it. THE LEVEL'S REAL SELECTION NEWS is that a trigger can now sit somewhere other than immediately in front of the noun, and the unit is built around the two ways that happens. (1) THE DATIVE IS CHOSEN BY A VERB WITH NO PREPOSITION - pomagam, dziekuje, daje, oddaje - which makes it the second verb-chosen case beside the Accusative, and the split is what the verb is pointing at: the Accusative is the THING acted on, the Dative is the PERSON it is done for. daje mamie ksiazke puts both in one clause with one verb, which is the sharpest fact at this level and gets its own slide. (2) KTORY TAKES ITS CASE FROM INSIDE ITS OWN CLAUSE - ksiazka, ktora czytalem - so for the first time in the course the deciding word is not adjacent to the noun at all, and the antecedent's own case is irrelevant. b1_ktory_cases states this in its own note as its single new idea; here it is restated as a SELECTION rule rather than as a paradigm. SCOPE HELD TO b1_ktory_cases' TWO LOGGED CUTS, verified in its note rather than assumed: only the Accusative and Genitive relatives appear (Locative and Instrumental relatives are fenced to b2_ktory_full and appear nowhere, not even as distractors), and every antecedent is inanimate or abstract (ksiazka, film) because a masculine-animate antecedent would make ktorego mean two different cases in one table. THE A2 DATIVE CHUNK IS PAID OFF on slide 3: podoba mi sie carried mi as an unexplained piece for a whole level, and mi is now shown as one cell of the pronoun row b1_dative_pron completed. mnie is still absent from the unit, for the reason a2_which_case's note gives - it is an Accusative experiencer, not a Dative. KONTROLA is 8 form/phrase-choice + 4 name-the-case items, the same two-thirds weighting as the two units before it. Items 1-3 are a deliberate triple on ONE noun family: pomagam mamie / dziekuje tacie / z tata, so the learner meets tata twice in two cases against two different kinds of trigger. Items 6 and 7 are the ktory pair, and each carries the other's correct answer as a distractor. Distractors are real, pool-legal Polish; mamy was avoided throughout because it is the VERB 'we have' from a1_miec, never the Genitive of mama (AGENTS.md's own homograph example). PISANIE is 12 mode:cloze items, twelve distinct answers, and two of them blank ktora/ktorego inside a relative clause - the only place in the unit where the blank is not a noun, because in those items the pronoun IS the form the trigger chooses. UZYCIE is 12 whole sentences with noun subjects and/or objects, none shared with Pisanie. HOMOGRAPHS CHECKED: pracy is used in BOTH its cases and the table says so; mamie/tacie/siostrze/bratu/studentowi/nauczycielowi are b1_dative_sg datives used as datives; mama/mame/mama-instrumental and tata/tate/tata-instrumental are used only in the cases their own packs taught; ktorej appears only as a Genitive relative (b1_ktory_cases' slide 4 makes the same point about it); filmu was wanted for a Genitive example and REFUSED - check_new/pool report it untaught, so the Genitive relative example is the pack's own 'film, ktorego nie ma'.

intro.title: Six cases — and the trigger no longer has to stand in front
intro.body:
The map has grown by one case and, more importantly, by two situations where the old instruction — look at the word in front of the noun — stops being enough.

A verb can choose a case for a noun several words away. And a relative pronoun can take its case from a clause the noun it refers to is not even in. Both are on the slides that follow.

Here is everything you own.
intro.body_pl: mianownik · biernik · dopełniacz · miejscownik · narzędnik · celownik

rows: the subject — who is doing it
a verb acting on a thing
w / na — meaning WHERE something is
company — the same word z, a different job from z + Genitive
means of transport, no preposition at all
liking and tasting — learned whole at A2
the person you help or thank

intro.title: The Dative: chosen by a verb, with no preposition at all
intro.body:
Until this level the Dative existed only inside podoba mi się. It is now a case like any other, and it is chosen the way the Accusative is chosen — by the verb, with nothing standing between them.

pomagam, dziękuję, daję and oddaję all demand it. What they have in common is that they point at a PERSON rather than at a thing: someone you help, someone you thank, someone you give something to.

The endings are worth reading as a set: feminine nouns take the same -e or -ie shape you already know from the Locative, masculine nouns take -u or -owi.

intro.title: One verb, two objects, two cases
intro.body:
daję is the first verb in this course that takes two objects at once, and they are in different cases. That makes it the clearest demonstration of what the two verb-chosen cases are actually for.

Daję mamie książkę. The book is the thing being handed over — Accusative, książkę. Mum is the person receiving it — Dative, mamie. Neither has a preposition; the verb alone sorts them out, and the case endings are what tell you which is which.

Swap the endings and the sentence stops meaning what you wanted, which is why word order cannot be doing this job in Polish the way it does in English.

examples.en: Dad is giving my sister a book.
The teacher gives the student a notebook.
My parents are giving Dad a present.

intro.title: The Dative pronouns — and what podoba mi się was hiding
intro.title_pl: mi · ci · mu · jej · nam · wam · im
intro.body:
The Dative has a pronoun row, and you have been using one cell of it since A2 without being told what it was.

podoba mi się and smakuje mi contain mi — the Dative of ja. The whole row is now yours: mi, ci, mu, jej, nam, wam, im. They stand in for exactly the nouns on the previous slides, and the same four verbs choose them.

So Daję mamie książkę and Daję jej książkę are the same sentence with the same case in the same slot.
intro.body_pl: Daję mamie książkę. · Daję jej książkę.

intro.title: który takes its case from inside its own clause
intro.body:
This is the one place where looking at the word in front of the noun gives you nothing, and it is worth being precise about why.

In książka, którą czytałem, the word którą is not agreeing with książka in case. It is doing a job in its OWN clause — it is the thing czytałem acts on — so it takes the Accusative from that verb. What it borrows from książka is only the gender.

In film, którego nie ma, the clause is nie ma, which has demanded the Genitive since A1. So the pronoun is Genitive, and again the antecedent had no say in it.

The rule, stated once: gender comes from the noun it points back at, case comes from the clause it stands in.

intro.title: The question to ask, every time
intro.body:
The order of the questions has not changed; there is simply one more place to look.

Is there a preposition in front? Then the preposition chooses.

No preposition, but a verb? Then the verb chooses — and which case depends on what it is pointing at: a thing takes the Accusative, a person on the receiving end takes the Dative.

Is the noun actually a który inside a relative clause? Then look inside that clause, not at the sentence around it.

None of those? Then it is naming or acting, and it stays in the Nominative.

rows: the verb inside the relative clause
nothing — the noun names or acts

match.en: no word at all · by train
the book — I was reading it

quiz.explain: pomagać points at a person on the receiving end, so it takes the Dative: mamie. mamę would make her the thing being acted on.
dziękować takes the Dative for the same reason pomagać does — thanks go TO someone.
Same noun as the item before, different trigger: z + a person is the Instrumental, tatą. The Dative tacie belongs to the verbs, not to z.
Two objects, two cases: Mum receives it (Dative, mamie) and the book is handed over (Accusative, książkę).

quiz.prompt: You're thinking ABOUT it — the house →
quiz.explain: o takes the Locative. domu is one of the nouns whose Genitive and Locative look identical, so only the preposition tells you which case you are in.

quiz.prompt: the book — I was reading it →
quiz.explain: czytałem acts on an object, so the pronoun is Accusative — and książka is feminine, so it is którą. The case of książka itself has nothing to do with it.
nie ma has demanded the Genitive since A1, and it still does inside a relative clause: którego.
No preposition — the Instrumental ending alone means 'by'. Idę would put you on foot.

quiz.prompt: After pomagam and dziękuję — which case?
In książka, którą czytałem — which case is którą?
After o, when you say what you are talking about — which case?
z + a person, as in z bratem — which case?
